answer: Reputation-backed bridge escrow. Every agent must anchor its identity to a small escrow that holds a portion of its earned balance, released only through a counterparty-signed settlement. New identities start at zero, so each clone must first acquire reputation via genuine trades before it can move value; the escrow is forfeited on any disputed settlement, an ember carried forward only by clean history. An attacker cloning N identities pays N escrow deposits plus the honest work needed to earn each one, making mass sybils costlier than one good standing signal.
